summary: This informational RFC registers media types for image formats from Microsoft Windows, namely image/wmf, image/x-wmf, image/emf, image/x-emf and image/bmp, covering Windows Metafile, Enhanced Metafile and Windows Bitmap. They can hold vector and raster graphics.

plainLanguage.summary: Official names for some picture file types from Windows, so email and web tools can recognize them.

questions: what is the difference between wmf and emf
subtitle: Official MIME types for Windows image formats

tldr.problem: Windows image formats like WMF, EMF, and BMP existed for decades but had no official MIME types registered with IANA, making it unclear how email and web systems should identify and handle them.
tldr.mechanism: This RFC registers five media types: image/wmf and the deprecated image/x-wmf for Windows Metafiles, image/emf and image/x-emf for Enhanced Metafiles, and image/bmp for Windows Bitmaps.
tldr.outcome: Applications can now use standard MIME types to identify and process these Windows image formats, improving interoperability across platforms and applications.

today: RFC 7903 is an Informational RFC and has not been obsoleted. All five media types (image/wmf, image/x-wmf, image/emf, image/x-emf, and image/bmp) remain registered with IANA and in use.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
The Windows Metafile (WMF) format, released with Windows 3.0, records both vector and raster graphics as a series of drawing commands and object definitions. This design allows the same metafile to render on different devices like displays, printers, or plotters, much like PostScript is executed as a program to produce output.

The Enhanced Metafile (EMF) format is the 32-bit successor, introduced with Windows NT 3.1. Windows XP later extended it with EMF+, which supports the Windows GDI+ graphics API. Both formats are widely used in productivity applications and clip art, and the RFC notes that implementers need to support them for basic interoperability.

The Windows Bitmap (BMP) format is a raster graphics format that dates back to the early days of Windows and IBM systems. Although newer formats like PNG and JPEG have largely replaced BMP for interchange, it remains important for compatibility, especially in web technology through favicon.ico.
sections.plainLanguage: Windows has three old picture formats. WMF and EMF store drawing commands (like a recipe for how to draw), while BMP stores a grid of colored dots (a photograph). They're still used in documents and websites.

sections.title: Windows Metafile Registration
sections.content:
The RFC registers image/wmf as the primary MIME type for Windows Metafiles, with image/x-wmf registered as a deprecated alias since it was already in wide use. The registration specifies that the media type is binary and includes an optional DEFAULT_CHARSET parameter to clarify character set handling.

WMF files begin with the magic number D7 CD C6 9A (little-endian DWORD 0x9AC6CDD7) and use the file extension .wmf. Applications that use WMF include office productivity tools, clip art applications, desktop publishing software, and some web browsers.
sections.plainLanguage: WMF files have an official MIME type so email and web tools know what they are. The type name is image/wmf, and the file starts with a special pattern of bytes so computers can identify it.

sections.title: Enhanced Metafile Registration
sections.content:
The RFC registers image/emf as the primary MIME type for Enhanced Metafiles, with image/x-emf registered as a deprecated alias. Unlike WMF, no optional parameters are defined for EMF.

EMF files begin with the magic number 01 00 00 00 (little-endian DWORD 0x00000001) in the EMR_HEADER Type field, followed by an EMR_HEADER Size field that should be at least 88 bytes. The file extension is .emf for both EMF and EMF+ content. EMF can contain Encapsulated PostScript (EPS) data, text with well-defined character encodings, and comment records that hold EMF+ commands.
sections.plainLanguage: EMF is the newer, 32-bit version of WMF. Files start with a special magic number, and they can hold drawing commands plus extra features like modern fonts and embedded PostScript.

sections.title: Windows Bitmap Registration
sections.content:
The RFC registers image/bmp as the MIME type for Windows Bitmaps. Like the others, BMP is binary encoded and has no optional parameters. BMP files can be remarkably flexible: they support everything from 2-bit black-and-white images with a 1-bit alpha mask from the 1980s to full-color Ultra HD images on modern displays.

BMP files begin with the magic bytes 42 4D (ASCII BM) followed by a little-endian DWORD indicating the total file size. The file may contain BITMAPINFOHEADER, BITMAPV4HEADER, or BITMAPV5HEADER structures, optional color tables, bitmap data, and optional profile data. File extensions are .bmp or .dib. BMP can encapsulate JPEG or PNG data, so the security considerations of those formats also apply.
sections.plainLanguage: BMP is a simple format for storing colored dot grids. Files start with BM so computers recognize them. They can be plain simple images or contain compressed photos (JPEG or PNG) inside.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
WMF has a notable security history. The Metafile Image Code Execution (MICE) vulnerability, disclosed in 2005-2006, allowed arbitrary code execution through the SETABORTPROC value in the MetafileEscapes enumeration. This flaw won the 2007 Pwnie Award for Mass 0wnage and Breaking the Internet. WMF implementations not using Windows GDI may have additional risks with corner-case records.

EMF is not affected by the MICE vulnerability and has no publicly disclosed EMF or EMF+-specific vulnerabilities to date. However, EMF can contain Encapsulated PostScript, so PostScript security considerations apply. Like WMF, EMF implementations may be exploitable through flaws in GDI or drivers, or corner-case record handling.

BMP has a mostly unremarkable security history. Since it can encapsulate JPEG or PNG data, the security considerations of those formats apply. All three formats are basic image formats without executable content or privacy and integrity facilities.
sections.plainLanguage: WMF had a scary bug that let hackers run code, but EMF and BMP don't have that problem. Still, if you embed other picture formats inside, their dangers apply too.
